• He determines the number of the stars: God's people can feel secure knowing the Lord cares for every detail of his creation. He knows all that belongs to him.

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: God delivers justice to both the poor and the wicked (Psalms 55:22; Psalms 140:12; Psalms 145:14; Psalms 146:7).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: Human achievements do not impress God, who commands nature. Instead, he finds joy in those who fear him.

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: God has complete authority and power over the weather (Psalms 77:17–18; Psalms 78:26; Psalms 104:4; Psalms 148:5–6).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: the legs of a man: Any physical or mental strength comes from the Lord, like the strength of a horse. These gifts are reasons to praise the Lord, not to boast (Jeremiah 9:23–24).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content:
• the bars of your gates: These represent protection from enemies. 

• God blesses his people by giving them safety, prosperity, peace, and the things they need (see Psalm 133:3).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: Simply by speaking his command, the Lord can change the season from harsh winter to refreshing spring (see Psalms 147:8; Psalms 148:5–6).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: word … statutes … judgments: The Lord gave powerful words to Israel so that they might obey him (Psalm 105:45).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the crowds welcomed him like a king and shouted blessings, including a phrase from this verse (Matthew 21:9; Mark 11:10; Luke 19:38).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: This psalm calls for the whole created order to praise the Lord because he has honored his faithful people.

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: The created order is stable because of the Lord's word (see Psalm 33:9).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: In the ancient Near East, people believed that different gods controlled different parts of nature. But the Lord rules over all of nature. Every part of creation serves him and brings him praise by obeying him (Psalms 77:17–18; Psalms 104:4; Psalms 135:7; Psalms 147:8, Psalms 147:15–18; Numbers 11:31).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: The psalmist calls all humans to offer praise to God, regardless of status, age, or gender.

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content:
• Praise of the Lord by all people is right because he is glorious and has blessed his people (see Psalm 147:13; Isaiah 46:13; Ephesians 3:10). 

• His saint are God's trusting and devoted servants (Psalm 86:2).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: This psalm of praise celebrates the Lord's victory. God is the Maker of Israel (Psalm 149:1–2) and the victorious King who shares his glory with his faithful followers (Psalms 149:3–9).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: God’s people, whom the world ignores and looks down on, will be shown to be right (Matthew 19:30). The humble will overcome those who oppress and persecute them (see Isaiah 61:3).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: vengeance: The Lord is the one who brings justice against wrongdoing (see Psalms 2:3; Psalms 94:1; Psalms 102:20; Psalms 142:7; Psalms 146:7).

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: The phrase mighty heavens refers to Genesis 1 and God's amazing work in filling the emptiness.

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: Everything that breathes is commanded to praise the Lord as he deserves. The whole Psalter describes the greatness of the Lord, so this psalm is a fitting conclusion.

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content:
• The psalmist calls all people to praise God with instruments and dancing.

• flutes: These are wind instruments (instruments you blow into to make sound). The Bible does not mention them as part of formal temple worship. This suggests they were used more in everyday life or celebrations, rather than in official worship at the temple.

• clashing cymbals: Temple musicians clapped two bronze bowls together to make a loud sound as part of the music.

entries.title: Psalms
entries.content: praise the LORD!: This refrain is a fitting conclusion to the entire book of Psalms.
